notes: Product: VS Code-first copilot embedded in ByteForge IDE. Primary ask: streaming completions with TTFT ~<40ms perceived by user; p50 <30ms, p95 <70ms for single-line completions. Concerned about jitter and backpressure when user types rapidly (multi-keystroke bursts). Wants token-budget tuning per buffer: different budgets for inline completion vs. multi-line suggestion vs. speculative completion. Discussed routing: pin to a specific model version for deterministic suggestions; fallback to quantized smaller model on high-load.
use_case_summary: Developer productivity plugin for enterprise customers — must feel instantaneous. Workloads: interactive completion, signature help, whole-function generation. Priority: minimize first-byte latency (TTFT) and limit jitter to avoid flicker in UI. Cost is important but secondary to UX for their paying customers. Will run a 2-week POC in internal teams followed by canary to 1k users.
technical_requirements: backpressure_handling: server push pause/resume on LSP/ws
token_budgeting: per-file and per-session budgets, speculative budget cap
model_pinning: ability to pin model-version per-deployment
fallback_policy: auto-fallback to smaller quantized model when sustained p95 latency > 200ms
poC_success_criteria: Avg TTFT improvement vs current infra >= 2x
No more than 2 user-facing backpressure events per 10k completions
Cost per active developer within estimated ARR model
commercial_notes: Interested in Dedicated pool to guarantee latency and isolate enterprise customers. Open to hosted API for early POC to speed integration. Asking for a blended cost model and committed monthly tokens for Dedicated discount.
sales_pitch_snippets: "If we can hit sub-40ms TTFT consistently, the product will feel native — that wins adoption." — Head of Product. Emphasize model pinning + predictable latency in deck.
legal_and_security_items: Need DPA + SOC2 report + KMS integration details. Data flow in extension: local buffer -> Redwood streaming endpoint (TLS) -> ephemeral KV cache. Ask about retention controls (turn off logs for snippets containing secrets).
implementation_notes: Plan: integrate Redwood streaming JS SDK into VS Code extension using websocket fallback. Start with hosted_api streaming with model pinning, then test Dedicated for latency SLA. Instrument token budget per-file and send budget hints in meta headers. Capture telemetry: TTFT, chunk sizes, socket reconnects, backpressure events.
risks: If we cannot reduce p95 latency under load, UX will regress and POC will fail. Potential legal delay around residency wording. Engineering bandwidth constrained in Q2.
final_comment: High strategic fit: developer-first company where perceived latency directly maps to retention. Priority to move POC to dedicated capacity early if hosted proves unpredictable under load.
